Subject: Pilot plan & ownership — Acme Logistics trial

Hi Olivia / Tom — great call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned owners before kickoff.

Summary of the discussion
- Goal: 2-week pilot to validate latency and cost targets for the routing/fulfillment assistant across a 10k monthly active user simulation.
- Key success criteria (proposed):
  1) 95th percentile generation latency < 450ms for 1k concurrent sessions
  2) Average cost per 1k tokens <= $X (TBD by finance)
  3) No P0 security issues discovered in pre-kickoff scan
  4) Integration tests pass for the prefix caching workflow (end-to-end)

RACI / owners (please confirm):
- Acme infra (network, VPN allowlist, firewall rules): Tom Bryce (Acme) [owner]
- App/product integration (API keys, test harness, sample data): Olivia Park (Acme) [owner]
- Security/compliance point of contact (for questionnaire & SOC evidence): Rachel Lee (Acme) [responsible]
- Redwood setup / runtime provisioning: Karthik Iyer (Redwood) [responsible]
- Commercial / procurement coordination: Monica Patel (Redwood) + Markus Klein (review)
- Success measurement & reporting: Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood, CS) [accountable]

Attachments: Acme_Pilot_RACI.xlsx (RACI template) and Pilot_Success_Criteria.md (detailed acceptance tests) attached. Also attached Redwood-POC-Environment-Checklist.pdf for infra preflight.

Proposed timeline
- Confirm owners & procurement contact by EOD 2026-03-22
- Redwood provisions test environment (short-lived dedicated pool) by 2026-03-27
- Integration window & test runs 2026-03-29 to 2026-04-09
- Pilot wrap / success review 2026-04-12

Action items for you
- Please confirm owners above or provide alternatives (reply-all)
- Share the procurement contact so we can send a light MSA/quote for this pilot

If that looks good I'll lock the kickoff meeting for Mon 2026-03-29, 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi all — jumping in from the tech side with a concise scoping checklist and clarifications on responsibility boundaries.

Technical preflight (what Redwood will deliver)
- Short-lived dedicated GPU pool (isolated) + preconfigured model variant for the trial
- Test API key(s) and a sample client harness for load generation
- Default KV/prefix caching enabled (configurable)
- Access logs and token-level latency traces for the pilot period

What we need from Acme
- Network allowlist + VPN endpoint details (Tom) — firewall rules for the Redwood IP range in the checklist
- Test dataset (anonymized) and a few example prompts/endpoints (Olivia)
- Point of contact for security evidence (Rachel) — we will share SOC2 artifact pointers and an export of runtime audit logs

RACI clarifications — proposed labels
- Responsible (does the work): Karthik (Redwood) for runtime; Tom (Acme) for infra
- Accountable (sign-off on success): Stephanie Nguyen (CS) — overall success metrics
- Consulted: Markus Klein (commercial) for any contractual scope changes
- Informed: Monica Patel (AE) and Olivia Park

Side notes and risk flags
- If Acme’s compliance scan requires an on-prem runner rather than a hosted pool, procurement lead should flag this ASAP — provisioning timelines change to ~3 weeks for private deployment.
- We will need a signed pilot MSA or PO before we start provisioning. Monica / Markus, can you coordinate with procurement once we have the contact?

I’ll attach a short environment checklist and the minimal network allowlist snippet. Happy to run a 30-minute tech kickoff for the infra leads next week.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

4) Kickoff & integration window: Mon 2026-03-29 — calendar invite to follow
